text:
support-jen: FYI — enterprise customer (private VPC) reports CORS preflight failures + intermittent 401s when calling our Node/TS SDK from a Vercel Edge function. They started seeing this after migrating billing (not sure if related). Logged with support ticket #8902.

devex-liam: Can you paste the minimal repro they used? browser vs edge runtime? exact SDK version?

support-jen: Repro summary from customer: they bundle @redwood/inference v0.8.1 into a Next.js Edge API route (middleware/runtime: edge). Calls fail in Safari and Chrome incognito sometimes. SDK call looks like: 

```ts
// edge api route (vercel edge)
import { Redwood } from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
export default async (req) => {
  const res = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-lite', prompt: 'hi' });
  return new Response(JSON.stringify(res));
};
```

They see console error: `Access to fetch at "https://api.redwood.inference/..." from origin "https://their-app.vercel.app" has been blocked by CORS policy: Request header field authorization is not allowed by Access-Control-Allow-Headers in preflight response.`
They also attached a server-side snippet where the same request (server to server) works fine.

eng-anna: Typical edge runtime issue: browser preflight happens client->our public API. If the browser adds `Authorization` on preflight, our CORS must expose that. Our public API should already allow `Authorization`, but two failure modes: 1) the browser isn't actually sending the token (e.g., runtime stripped header) and some gateway returns 401 without CORS headers; 2) a middleware or proxy (on their side or vercel) strips `authorization` on preflight so the preflight fails. Do we have the actual network traces from their browser?

support-jen: They attached a HAR showing preflight `OPTIONS` to `/v1/generate` returned 401 and no `Access-Control-Allow-Headers`. HAR snippet: 

```
OPTIONS /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.inference
Origin: https://their-app.vercel.app
Access-Control-Request-Method: POST
Access-Control-Request-Headers: authorization, content-type

HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json
{ "error": "unauthenticated" }
```

devex-liam: That response explains it: OPTIONS returned 401 with no CORS headers. We should never 401 preflight. Preflight must be handled unauthenticated and return the CORS allow headers. Why would our gateway 401 an OPTIONS? Two guesses: (A) the edge SDK is sending a cookie/session or auth probe to the gateway and gateway enforces auth for OPTIONS (bad config), (B) a stage/proxy in front of our public CORS handler is enforcing auth because the request method is seen as non-simple.

eng-max: Quick repro I ran locally with `fetch` from a service worker showed identical behavior when the upstream auth middleware attempted to validate `Authorization` on OPTIONS. The fix is to short-circuit OPTIONS in the ingress layer (return 204 + CORS headers) before auth. I looked at the gateway rules and there's a recent commit that added an auth check in the ingress lambda — apparently it didn't whitelist `OPTIONS`. Rolling back that check for preflight will fix customer-facing failures.

infra-olga: Oof — that ingress change was deployed in Friday's infra rollout (deploy-bot: 1765432200). I flagged it but it went through canary. I'll open a rollback.

deploy-bot: [deploy] rollback-requested: ingress-auth-guard (triggered by infra-olga).

eng-anna: While infra rolls back, we should also offer a workaround to the customer: they can proxy requests through a server runtime (API route on serverless Node) instead of Edge, or they can use a signed short-lived token in a query param (not ideal) while we fix. Also confirm SDK packaging: edge builds should import the ESM/browser entrypoint which avoids injecting Node fetch polyfills that can change header behavior. Which bundler target did they use?

support-jen: Customer uses next.config.js with `experimental.edge: { ... }` and uses Vercel default bundler. They didn't intentionally polyfill. They did say Safari had more failures than Chrome.

devex-liam: Safari's preflight can be stricter. Two more checks: 1) confirm they aren't using an app-level ServiceWorker that reissues the OPTIONS and drops headers; 2) check whether Vercel's edge runtime rewrites `Authorization` on preflight. I have a short curl repro you can forward: 

```
# from customer's machine (simulate browser preflight):
curl -i -X OPTIONS 'https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate' \
  -H 'Origin: https://their-app.vercel.app' \
  -H 'Access-Control-Request-Method: POST' \
  -H 'Access-Control-Request-Headers: authorization, content-type'
```

If that returns 401 + no CORS headers, it's definitively ingress.

eng-max: Also found a secondary issue: older SDK bundles (<=0.8.1) ship a tiny helper that tries to detect runtime and may call a background probe to validate key on import; if that probe makes a `OPTIONS`-like request or triggers gateway auth checks, it could cause races. That was fixed in 0.8.3 by removing the probe in edge/browser builds. Recommend customer try 0.8.3-canary or we can hotfix 0.8.3 asap.

eng-anna: Good catch. We should do two things: 1) infra rollback to restore preflight-shortcircuiting; 2) publish 0.8.3 patch that removes probes on import and ensures the browser ESM entrypoint doesn't call fetch on module load.

infra-olga: Rollback in progress, ETA ~10m. I will post when done.

support-jen: I told the customer to run the `curl` preflight test and to switch to a server-side proxy as a short-term workaround. Also asked them to try the canary SDK. They said they can test in morning (their timezone).

deploy-bot: [deploy] rollback-complete: ingress-auth-guard (1765432302).

eng-anna: Rollback done — ingress now returns 204 + CORS headers for OPTIONS. That will unblock preflight. I also created PR #1245 to remove auth check for preflight and added unit tests.

eng-max: I've cut canary release `@redwood/inference@0.8.3-canary.1` which removes the import-time probe. If customer wants to try quickly: `npm i @redwood/inference@0.8.3-canary.1` in their edge bundle and redeploy.

devex-liam: For future prevention, add an infra integration test that simulates browser preflight hitting the edge ingress (OPTIONS with authorization header) and assert we return proper CORS headers even when upstream auth is enabled. Also add an SDK unit test ensuring no network calls on import for the edge/browser entrypoint.

support-jen: Thanks team — I'll update ticket #8902 with the rollback and canary. Customer asked also about billing note: they said failures coincided with billing migration but that looks like timing of our infra rollout, not billing itself.

eng-anna: Agreed. Closing loop once customer confirms. Please ping here with results. :thumbsup:

support-jen: Will do — marking follow-up for tomorrow.
